Problem and representative equations The formula uses a scalar Itô SDE. a is drift, b is diffusion and ΔWₙ are independent Gaussian increments with mean zero and variance Δt. Algorithm Generate Wiener increments and advance deterministic and stochastic terms. Strong-error refinement must couple paths by summing fine increments into the coarse increment. Weak error concerns expectations of test functions, not the discrepancy of one pair of paths. Conditions and pitfalls Under suitable global Lipschitz, moment and smoothness assumptions, Euler–Maruyama typically has strong order 1/2 and weak order 1. Superlinear growth or positivity constraints can invalidate the method and require specialized treatments. Sampling uncertainty may dominate weak discretization error. What to check Use geometric Brownian exact paths and Ornstein–Uhlenbeck moments to test strong and weak convergence separately. Record step size, random streams, sample count and uncertainty, including negative states or boundary violations.
